questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: First of all, I highly appreciated the surrounding nature of Vancouver in choosing my study destination since I am a big fan of nature, hiking, and other outdoor activities. Second, I enjoyed the big variety of available courses on UBC. This gave me great opportunities of expanding my study field with completely new perspectives and insights. Also, I wanted to go to a prestigious university with a high academic level. Lastly, I chose Vancouver since I wanted to attend university in an english speaking country so I could improve my english proficiency.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy. I think UBC provided good guidance and information trough their informative emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: On our first day (Imagine Day) we were assigned to a group and had a student advisor who showed us around campus. Afterwards we had the opportunity to attend some presentations with information on both academic and social aspects of studying on UBC, e.g., how to add and drop courses, what clubs to join, etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Exchange students were placed in two different residences on campus (Fairview Crescent and Walter Gage) in either 4-people or 6-people shared flats.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: For residents in the residences which exchange students were assigned to there was no real meal plans. Though, one could sign up for a value plan which gave us 5% on selected places to eat. In residence we had good cooking facilities with stove and oven. Unfortunately, there was no utilities in the apartment when we moved in so we had to buy everything for the kitchen ourselves - this was a minus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Campus housing is a great place to live, close to campus and beautiful nature and green areas! Though, if you are a person who enjoy the buzzling city, campus if a bit far away - around 40 minutes in bus, but the public transit runs just fine!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: During the first two weeks of school you have the opportunity of adding and dropping courses, so you could try out different courses and thereafter decide on which courses you would like.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Go Global was helpful in providing information, and the UBC website also contains a lot of helpful information - not only with regard to the course registration process but also all other aspects of UBC life.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It went pretty smoothly for me. I only had to drop and add one course, and I was very lucky to get the last seat in the course which I added.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you find yourself really wanting a course but it's full, my advice would be to contact the professor. Often you can get on a waiting list (during the first two weeks people will drop courses and seats will be available) or they are willing to open op an extra seat in the course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had two 100-courses and two 200-courses. I found the academic level of my courses quite easy but also challenging in some aspects since the way of 'doing school' in Canada is very different from how we do it in DK.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Overall, I liked the teaching style at UBC. My professors were very engaged. They often encouraged to discussion and reflection and wanted us to participate in the classes - sometimes a bit too much, though. In terms of the exams, I found it a lot more about memorizing than critically reflecting, discussing, and likewise, on relevant topics. This way, it was very different from what I am used to from UCPH. But it was refreshing and nice to experience!

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
SOCI 101 Social Interaction and Culture 
SOCI 260 Work and Society 
INFO 100 (De)coding Information and Why It Matters
FMST 210 Family Context of Human Development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend SOCI 260 and INFO 100.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Only a few days before my departure to Canada, I was unaware that my roomies and I had to buy all stuff for the kitchen. This was certainly an unexpected cost.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most items was more expensive than expected. Canada is an expensive country to live in.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of non-academic opportunities was available. There is a wide range of different clubs to join on UBC! Especially there is great sport opportunities on campus.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I have nothing to recommend since I did not participate in any non-academic activities other than a few times of drop-in iceskating. Therefore, instead I recommend that you actually join some!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you like nature, I recommend that you use the nature around Vancouver and do some hike! There is so many spectacular hikes around Vancouver. Also, I highly recommend going to Banff and Whistler!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. Canadians are so friendly, nice, and polite! It makes it easy to adjust to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people in your classes! It is nice to have a friend in class and to get to know lots of different people from different countries.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: To be honest, I did not really find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and thoughtfulness of the Canadian people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Socialize, make new friends (not only other Danish students even though it seems secure), 2) If you have the slightest interest, join a club, sport activities or other non-academic activities, 3) Make sure to have fun; explore the city and the amazing nature!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Can't think of anything at the moment.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know so many new people from all around the world - it makes me feel very lucky.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing those at home and finding a good balance between schoolwork and having fun.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
